captions.instagram:
What are the laws of thermodynamics?

Heat flows downhill, energy always balances, no engine is perfect and absolute zero is out of reach. Watch hot and cold molecules share their speed, push a piston with a heater, run Carnot's perfect engine, pump heat uphill with an AC, and meet Maxwell's demon.

→ Hot and cold boxes touch. Fast molecules share their energy until both reach one temperature.
→ First law: heat in equals the gas’s energy gain plus the work it does. ΔU = Q − W.
→ Lift the wall and the gas spreads. Only reversing every molecule could ever put it back.
→ Heat does work only as it flows from hot to cold, and some must always be dumped.
→ A car engine: Carnot allows 88%, the ideal cycle 60%, real engines about 30%.

youtubeLong.description:
Heat flows downhill, energy always balances, no engine is perfect and absolute zero is out of reach. Watch hot and cold molecules share their speed, push a piston with a heater, run Carnot's perfect engine, pump heat uphill with an AC, and meet Maxwell's demon.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/e/thermoclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/thermoclear

In this video:
• Temperature is jiggling, and heat flows downhill. Air molecules at 20 °C fly at about 500 m/s.
• The energy books: ΔU = Q − W. Heat a gas under a piston and part of the heat raises its internal energy while the rest pushes the piston as work.
• No engine can be perfect. Heat does work only while flowing from hot to cold, and some must always be dumped.
• Pumping heat uphill costs work. An AC or fridge moves heat from cold to hot and pays in electricity.
• Entropy, the demon and absolute zero. Spread-out arrangements vastly outnumber tidy ones, so entropy grows.
